eyebrow: SOC Operations, SIEM & Log Analysis · Chapter 7
subtitle: Lesson 25 · SOAR & Automation Basics

steps.label: Orchestration
steps.sub: connects the SIEM, EDR, threat intel, and ticketing tools together via APIs

steps.label: Automation
steps.sub: runs the same repeatable steps every time, without a human doing each one

steps.label: Response
steps.sub: takes the real action itself -- block, quarantine, isolate -- not just an alert

code:
SIEM alone:
  Suspicious login detected -> alert raised -> waits for an analyst

SIEM + SOAR:
  Suspicious login detected -> alert raised
  -> SOAR checks IP against threat intel
  -> if malicious: isolate the host automatically
  -> analyst notified either way
caption: Response is the piece a SIEM alone never does -- it stops at telling a human.

code:
Alert volume:      climbing every year (more endpoints, more log sources)
Analyst headcount: growing far more slowly, if at all

Result: alert fatigue -- too many alerts, not enough analyst time
caption: SOAR doesn't fix the gap by adding people -- it removes the repeatable work from the analyst's plate.
